appraisal_events.evidence: Saint-Loup delivers an extended, erudite disquisition on military strategy, citing philosophy, history (Ulm, Mack), and cavalry doctrine; an unnamed dinner companion affirms 'Saint-Loup a raison et il est probable que le prochain Service en Campagne portera la trace de cette évolution.'
appraisal_events.explanation: The passage is dominated by Saint-Loup's articulate, wide-ranging exposition, rendered at length and approvingly agreed with by his companion, which elevates his standing as an intellectually authoritative and persuasive figure.

appraisal_events.evidence: After Saint-Loup jokingly remarks that his friend's opinions seem to impress the narrator more than his own, the narrator reassures him: 'Ne sois pas si susceptible... Je t'ai écouté avec assez d'avidité!'
appraisal_events.explanation: Saint-Loup briefly betrays touchiness at his friend's rapport with the narrator; the narrator immediately counters this with a direct affirmation of eager attention, restoring Saint-Loup's confidence in their bond.

status_effects.explanation: Saint-Loup's lengthy, sophisticated military exposition, affirmed by his companion, clearly elevates his local rhetorical and intellectual authority.
A momentary flicker of jealousy or touchiness in Saint-Loup is resolved by the narrator's warm reassurance, leaving him locally reaffirmed rather than diminished.

ambiguities: The narrator explicitly presents two competing readings of Saint-Loup's joking remark about his friend impressing the narrator more ('soit que cette sympathie naissante... l'agaçât un peu, soit qu'il trouvât gentil de la consacrer'), leaving it uncertain whether this reflects genuine jealousy or mere amused approval, which affects how much (if any) diminishment to attribute to Saint-Loup in that moment.
